_meta.indication: YERVOY (ipilimumab) is indicated for the treatment of unresectable or metastatic melanoma.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind, three-arm trial randomizing patients 3:1:1 to ipilimumab + gp100, ipilimumab monotherapy, or gp100 vaccine alone
pivotal_trials.population: HLA-A2*0201-positive patients with previously treated unresectable stage III or stage IV malignant melanoma
pivotal_trials.result: Ipilimumab monotherapy vs gp100: HR=0.66 (95% CI 0.51, 0.87), p=0.0026; median OS 10.22 vs 6.44 months. Ipilimumab+gp100 vs gp100: HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.55, 0.85), p=0.0004; median OS 9.95 vs 6.44 months.

nct_ctgov.title: MDX-010 Antibody, MDX-1379 Melanoma Vaccine, or MDX-010/MDX-1379 Combination Treatment for Patients With Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized (1:1), double-blind, two-arm trial of dacarbazine plus ipilimumab 10 mg/kg versus dacarbazine plus placebo in patients with untreated unresectable stage III or IV melanoma; provided corroborative replication of the MDX010-20 overall survival effect.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with untreated unresectable AJCC stage III or metastatic (stage IV) melanoma who had received no prior systemic therapy for metastatic or unresectable disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (primary endpoint; amended from progression-free survival)
pivotal_trials.result: High-level survival results demonstrated that treatment with ipilimumab resulted in improved survival, providing replication of the treatment effect observed in MDX010-20.

nct_ctgov.title: Dacarbazine and Ipilimumab vs. Dacarbazine With Placebo in Untreated Unresectable Stage III or IV Melanoma

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) are fatigue, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, and colitis. In Study 1 (3 mg/kg arm): diarrhea 32% (Grade 3-5 5%), colitis 8% (Grade 3-5 5%), pruritus 31%, rash 29%. The major risks are severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions, including immune-mediated enterocolitis (Grade 3-5 in 7%), hepatitis, dermatitis, neuropathy, and endocrinopathy (Grade 3-4 in 1.8%).
target_moa: Ipilimumab is a fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that blocks cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4, CD152); by blocking the binding of CTLA-4 to the B7 molecules (CD80/CD86) on antigen-presenting cells it potentiates T-cell activation and the anti-tumor immune response.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: IMMUNE-MEDIATED ADVERSE REACTIONS — YERVOY can result in severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions due to T-cell activation and proliferation, which may involve any organ system; the most common severe reactions are enterocolitis, hepatitis, dermatitis (including toxic epidermal necrolysis), neuropathy, and endocrinopathy.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved; it evaluates healthcare providers' understanding of the serious risks of YERVOY and the management of immune-mediated adverse reactions.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; FDA did not seek ODAC advice because demonstration of overall survival in two controlled clinical trials provided sufficient evidence of clinical benefit.

summary.text: YERVOY received a traditional (regular) approval under priority review for unresectable or metastatic melanoma, based on improved overall survival in randomized trial MDX010-20 with corroborative replication from trial CA184024; it had orphan drug designation for melanoma and was approved with a REMS. No advisory committee was convened because overall survival in two controlled trials provided sufficient evidence of clinical benefit.

requirement.text: Assess anti-drug antibody (ADA) and neutralizing ADA responses to ipilimumab in at least 300 ipilimumab-treated patients enrolled in the required postmarketing trial (PMR 6).

citations.quote: To conduct an assessment of anti-drug antibody (ADA) response and neutralizing ADA responses to ipilimumab with a validated assay (required in PMR 2 and 3) capable of sensitively detecting ADA responses in the presence of ipilimumab levels that are expected to be present at the time of patient sampling. The ADA response will be evaluated in at least 300 ipilimumab-treated patients enrolled in the required postmarketing trial (PMR 6) comparing 3 mg/kg versus 10 mg/kg of ipilimumab monotherapy.

requirement.text: During the required 3 mg/kg vs 10 mg/kg monotherapy trial (PMR 6), obtain comprehensive baseline DNA sample acquisition (>=95% of ITT) and conduct pharmacogenomic analyses assessing CD86 gene polymorphisms as determinants of immune-mediated adverse events.

citations.quote: During the conduct of the required postmarketing trial comparing 3mg/kg vs. 10mg/kg ipilimumab monotherapy (PMR 6), you will obtain comprehensive baseline DNA sample acquisition (\ge 95\% of ITT) and conduct pharmacogenomic association analyses to assess the potential clinical utility of CD86 gene polymorphisms as genetic determinants of immune mediated adverse events.

requirement.text: Following assessment of data from Trial CA184024, design and conduct a trial comparing efficacy (primary endpoint overall survival) and safety of ipilimumab 3 mg/kg vs 10 mg/kg monotherapy every three weeks for four doses in unresectable Stage III or Stage IV melanoma.

citations.quote: Following the assessment of data from Trial CA184024, you will design and conduct a trial to compare the efficacy, with the primary endpoint of overall survival and the safety of ipilimumab at doses of 3mg/kg versus 10mg/kg given as monotherapy every three weeks for four doses in patients with unresectable Stage III or Stage IV melanoma.

requirement.text: Identify further genetic determinants of immune-mediated adverse events caused by ipilimumab using DNA samples from the required 3 mg/kg vs 10 mg/kg monotherapy study for genome-wide association analyses.

citations.quote: To identify further genetic determinants of immune-mediated adverse events caused by ipilimumab. DNA samples from the required postmarketing study comparing 3 mg/kg vs. 10 mg/kg ipilimumab monotherapy will be used to conduct genome-wide association analyses. The design of these analyses will be reviewed by FDA and a final report with electronic datasets will be provided.
